Description: The Maxine Goodman Levin School of Urban Affairs at Cleveland State University is consistently recognized as one of the best public affairs colleges in the nation. The Master of Public Administration (MPA) program prepares students to lead in diverse and dynamic urban environments. Its mission is to advance intellectual and administrative leadership in public administration by preparing students to assume the challenges of public service. The program is committed to leadership development, to finding solutions to community problems, and to an enhanced understanding of public policy and management in a diverse society. By applying engaged and interactive learning, faculty and students work together to discover, generate, share, and extend intellectual resources for the benefit of the community. Coursework provides a foundation in public service, administration, and management with specialized skills grounded in one of the program's areas of expertise. Curriculum areas include organizational and managerial skills and practices, political and legal institutions and processes, economic and social systems, concepts and techniques of financial administration, nonprofit management, techniques of analysis (quantitative, economic, statistical methods, and computer systems), human resources management, and diversity, equity, and inclusion. The program is comprised of 40 credit hours, including core courses, an area of specialization, electives, and a capstone. It is multidisciplinary, drawing on faculties from the Monte Ahuja College of Business, the Levin College of Urban Affairs, and the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law. The principal objective is to prepare graduates for administrative positions in government, nonprofit, and public-service organizations, providing a broad educational base as well as specific administrative techniques. The program is designed for both in-service students and recent college graduates seeking public service careers, with most courses offered in the evening and some online for flexibility.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs and Administration (NASPAA).

Description: Imagulation of the Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (MSEE) degree program at Cleveland State University (CSU) equips students to advance in this dynamic and evolving industry with the knowledge needed to thrive. The program integrates theory and applications through courses designed for students planning to continue their studies at the doctoral level, as well as those who do not intend to pursue formal studies beyond the master's degree. Each student plans a program of study tailored to their goals and interests in consultation with an advisor appointed by the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. Students have the option to specialize in areas such as Communication systems, Computer systems, Control systems, Nanobiotechnology, and Power electronics and power systems. The program features flexibility for working professionals, offering courses in the late afternoon and early evening, and options to study part-time or full-time. Research opportunities are available through course-only, thesis track (6 credit hours of master's research), or project option (4 credit hours of project). The MSEE Program Curriculum entails coursework requirements of 32 credit hours for the course-only option, or 30 credit hours for the thesis option (including 6 credit hours of research and 24 credit hours of coursework) or project option (including 4 credit hours of project and 24 credit hours of coursework).

Department: College of Education and Human Services
Description: At Cleveland State University, the Early Childhood (P–5) Education Program prepares future educators to support the learning and development of children from birth through grade 5. The P–5 program emphasizes developmentally appropriate practice, relationship-building, and deep engagement with schools. Through immersive coursework and hands-on fieldwork, students learn to design and deliver child-centered instruction, build supportive learning environments, partner effectively with families and communities, and advocate for the needs of young learners in schools and society. Graduates earn a bachelor's or master's degree and an Ohio P–5 teaching license—ready to lead classrooms, partner with families, and make a meaningful difference in the lives of young children. Students complete more than 700 hours of clinical training, working in classrooms and early childhood settings across Northeast Ohio. CSU has deep, long-standing relationships with educational partners—and hosts three public schools on its own campus, giving students daily, real-time access to vibrant classrooms and mentor teachers. The program supports the social, emotional, cognitive, and physical development of all learners, including children from a wide range of cultural, language, and ability backgrounds. The P-5 Program offers undergraduate and graduate courses for individuals who are preparing to teach young children. It is designed for students who are interested in fulfilling leadership roles in early childhood facilities. The purpose of the program is to prepare graduates to implement developmentally appropriate curriculum for children from birth to age ten. Students develop skills needed to support culturally, linguistically, and ability diverse children and their families. The Early Childhood Education (ECE) Program is committed to a broad range of clinical experiences, long-term development of the whole child, child-initiated learning, culturally responsive practices, and a collaborative developmentally appropriate approach to education. Rigorous preparation helps to include the likelihood that students will be hired upon graduation.

Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies curriculum takes full advantage of its location in a major urban setting in fulfilling its commitment to urban education, research, and community service. Students pursuing the Bachelor of Arts degree program take courses and seminars dealing directly with urban problems and their solutions. The Urban Studies major entails the study of America's cities, metropolitan areas, and their people.
